subject: Concord AI dedicated capacity request — proposal & prioritization
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@concord.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@concord.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for Concord Q4 peak — initial ask

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look. We're planning to take production traffic on our recommendation engine in late Q3 and expect a strong ramp through Q4. Early traffic models put peak demand at ~1,500 A100-hours/month non-preemptible for inference with an expected 2x burst window during launches. We want a dedicated pool with predictable latency and the ability to burst for 48-hour launch windows.

Attached is a draft SOW showing our expected throughput distribution and an initial runway for 12 months. Key asks: 1) guaranteed non-preemptible baseline (committed), 2) burst capacity on top of baseline, 3) 99.9% SLA for inference latency during business-critical windows.

Can you confirm feasibility and a ballpark committed pricing for 12-month term? If helpful, we can line up procurement + engineering call this week.

Thanks,
Beth Carter
Head of ML Ops, Concord AI
[Attachment: Concord_SOW_draft.pdf (PDF)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@concord.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for Concord Q4 peak — initial ask

Beth — appreciate the SOW and the clear ask. Short answer: feasible, but there are trade-offs to lock in 1,500 non-preemptible A100-hours/month depending on start date and commit length.

High-level proposal for conversation:
- Reserved baseline: 1,125 A100-hours/month (75% of peak) as the committed pool.
- Burst credits: mechanism to purchase or consume up to an additional 750 A100-hours in 48-hr launch windows (pay-as-you-burst or pre-bought credits).
- SLA: 99.9% latency within reserved windows; burst lanes are best-effort but we can guarantee spot capacity during scheduled launch windows with a short-term reservation.

I'll attach a quick capacity model to show how the math looks across our fleet for your requested timeframe. Marissa, Karthik — looping you both in to confirm pricing tier and whether we can accommodate Concord's requested non-preemptible baseline without impacting current commitments.

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to align.

— Jonas
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_model.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@concord.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for Concord Q4 peak — commercial framing

Beth — thanks for the outline. From a commercial perspective we can offer a 12-month reserved contract that maps to Jonas' proposed 75% baseline. Proposed commercial terms (draft):
- Commitment: 75% baseline (1,125 A100-hours/month) at a 28% discount to list for a 12-month commit.
- Burst credits: option to buy a block of credits upfront for a further 20% discount vs on-demand burst pricing.
- Onboarding fee (one-time) to cover dedicated onboarding and perf tuning.

Before we send a formal SOW, quick note on prioritization: we have two other near-term reserved deals (Lighthouse and Aperture) with overlapping Q3-Q4 launch windows. Ops will need to validate if honoring Concord's baseline as-is will require reassigning preemptible lanes or pushing Lighthouse's ramp. Karthik — are you able to run a quick contention check?

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Beth Carter <beth.carter@concord.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for Concord Q4 peak — ops impact and recommendation

Marissa / Jonas / Beth,

I ran the model against current fleet allocations and the near-term deal slate. Key findings:
- Fleet headroom in the US region is limited in the Oct-Nov window (roughly 16% raw free capacity).
- Current reserved commitments (Lighthouse, Aperture) consume ~70% of projected production baseline for Q4.
- To guarantee Concord's 1,125 non-preemptible baseline starting Sep 15 without adding hardware, we would: either (A) convert ~4 preemptible slots in the US pool to non-preemptible, or (B) delay Lighthouse's full ramp by ~6 weeks. Both options have customer/contract implications.

Our recommendation (to balance revenue, SLA risk, and operational friction):
1) Offer Concord the 75% reserved baseline with firm start date and a 48-hour scheduled launch reservation for burst needs.
2) Provide burst credits as a paid add-on with a defined booking window for launch events (so we can guarantee capacity).
3) If Concord requires immediate unplanned non-preemptible capacity beyond the baseline, require a runway extension or buyout clause to compensate affected customers.

Attached is a one-page priority matrix I used to score deals (ARR, SLA tier, historical ramp fidelity, strategic importance). This is the metric set ops will use when adjudicating tight windows.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Dedicated Operations
[Attachment: priority_matrix.pdf (PDF)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@concord.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for Concord Q4 peak — final commercial offer

Beth — thanks for your patience while we validated the fleet impact. Based on ops guidance, here's the offer we can move forward with: 

Summary offer:
- Reserved baseline: 1,125 A100-hours/month (75% of peak) — 12-month commitment — 28% discount.
- Burst: 750 A100-hours of burst credits available for purchase at a discounted block rate; Concord may book up to two 48-hour guaranteed launch reservations per quarter (requires 72-hr advance notice).
- SLA: 99.9% latency within reserved windows; burst reservations carry a service-level booking guarantee.
- Compensation clause: If Concord requests immediate, unplanned conversion of preemptible capacity into non-preemptible at contract start, a one-time buyout will be required to make affected parties whole.

Next steps: I will prep the SOW with the above terms and Marissa will route it to procurement. If that looks good, sign via DocuSign (link below) and we’ll schedule technical onboarding with Karthik's team for the week of Sep 6.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/CONC-SOW-2027

Thanks — let me know if you'd like to jump on a final 20-min call to walk the SOW.

— Jonas
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
